query: South Korea KOSPI foreign investor net buy/sell value weekly latest June 2026, recent trend in trillion won
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings on KOSPI foreign investor net buy/sell flows:

## Latest Data (as of mid-July 2026)

**Most recent daily flows:**
- **July 15, 2026:** Foreign investors reversed to **net BUYING +2.03 trillion won**, driving an 8.15% rebound to 7,415.38
- **July 13, 2026:** Foreign **net SOLD −1.71 trillion won** as KOSPI crashed −8.95% below 7,000

**Weekly-scale figure (best available):** Foreign investors sold roughly **28 trillion won (~$19 billion) net over eight consecutive sessions** (late June through July 7), before briefly reversing to net buying July 8–9. No single official "weekly" KRX figure was published in the sources, so this 8-session total is the closest weekly proxy.

**Cumulative record (the headline story):**
- **YTD through July 3:** −157.3 trillion won (~$102.5 billion) — a record
- **First half (Jan–Jun 2026):** −148.32 trillion won, ~90% concentrated in Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix

## Key Trend Context
- The massive selling occurred **despite** a ~91.9% YTD KOSPI surge — framed by the Korea Exchange CEO as **portfolio rebalancing/profit-taking**, not loss of confidence.
- A **weak won (~1,555/USD)** amplified dollar-based selling incentives.
- Foreign ownership actually **rose to 40.47%** (from 36.65% in January) as price gains outpaced the value of selling.
- Retail investors net bought ~104.8 trillion won in H1 as a counterbalance.
- Brokerages expected selling pressure to persist into H2 2026.

The report has been delivered with full sourcing (Korea Exchange data via Korea Times, Korea JoongAng Daily, Seoul Economic Daily, CNBC, Bloomingbit, and Seoul Closing Bell) and structured data points covering daily, weekly, and cumulative timeframes.
